author_note: Refund chase plus an address change plus a newsletter gripe. Primary ask is contested.
text: Hi, three things really. The refund for the Ashford throw (order 51204) still hasn't landed and it's been two weeks. Also I've moved so can you update my address to 14 Bellweather Rise, Leeds LS8 2QR for anything still coming. And please stop the marketing emails, I get about four a week. Thanks, Marta

author_note: Faulty item buried under a delivery question. Safety-adjacent but not stated as harm.
text: Order 49877 - the second box never turned up, courier says delivered but it isn't here. Separately the floor lamp that DID arrive has a wobbly base, it tipped over when the cat brushed past it. Do I need to send it back or will you send a replacement base?

author_note: Cancellation window plus a payment double-charge. Two different urgencies in one ticket.
text: I need to cancel order 52310 please, I only placed it an hour ago and I've realised I ordered the wrong size rug. Also I think I've been charged twice, there are two pending amounts on my card for £64.99 each.

author_note: Praise wrapped around a real operational ask. Tests the feedback_and_complaint boundary.
text: First of all the linen cushions are gorgeous, genuinely the nicest thing in the room. Second, less gorgeous, the matching bolster never arrived. Order 50118. Any idea where it is?

author_note: Heavy typos, routine delivery chase.
text: hi wher is my ordr 48293 pls its ment to arive tusday and nuthing yet, can u chek for me thnx

author_note: Typos plus abbreviations, refund policy question, low urgency.
text: whats ur retruns policy? bougt a mirror last mnth n it dosnt fit the space, can i still snd it bk? no damge to it

author_note: Keyword-mode fragment, minimal context. Genuinely thin.
text: invoice 8841 copy pls

author_note: Typos masking a payment failure.
text: cant chekout, card keeps geting declind but my bank sez its fine?? tryed 3 times now. order for the oak side tbale

author_note: Ordinary frustration, NOT severe anger. Tests the anger bar in the brief.
text: This is the third time I've had to email about order 47156. Nobody has replied to either of my previous messages. I'm getting really tired of this. Where is my delivery?

author_note: Severe: sustained abuse and profanity at staff. Should escalate.
text: Absolutely useless shower of idiots. Two months, TWO MONTHS, and you still can't deliver one bloody bookcase. Whoever is running your logistics wants sacking. I've had enough of your pathetic excuses and your useless staff. Sort it out or I'm done.

author_note: Loud but the underlying ask is routine and low urgency. Tests urgency vs anger separation.
text: WHY do I keep getting your emails?? I have unsubscribed FOUR TIMES. Take me off your list. This is harassment at this point.

author_note: Calm wording, explicit statement of ending the relationship. Borderline severe.
text: I've been a customer for six years and spent a lot of money with you. After the way this return has been handled I won't be ordering again and I'll be closing my account. I'd like someone to tell me why the refund was reduced by £18 without warning.

author_note: Supplier sales pitch. Out of scope.
text: Hello, I represent Vantage Freight Solutions. We work with mid-sized ecommerce retailers to reduce last-mile delivery costs by up to 30%. Would your operations lead be available for a 15-minute call next week? Happy to send over a deck.

author_note: Job application to the support inbox. Out of scope.
text: Dear Sir/Madam, I am writing to apply for any available positions in your warehouse or customer service team. I have four years of retail experience and am available immediately. My CV is attached. Kind regards, Danny O.

author_note: Wrong company entirely.
text: I'm chasing a boiler service that was booked for the 14th and nobody came. The engineer was supposed to call ahead. This is the second missed appointment. Reference HB-20119.

author_note: Genuine customer, but asking something the support team has no remit over.
text: Do you know whether the Ashford range is manufactured in a factory that uses organic cotton certification, and could you send me the audit reports for your dye suppliers? I'm writing a piece on textile supply chains.

author_note: No order reference, no clear ask. Could be delivery, could be refund.
text: It still hasn't been sorted out. You said last week it would be. Can someone actually deal with this please.

author_note: Could be account_access or account_management. Deliberately underdetermined.
text: I can't get into my account. I think I might have set it up with my work email originally but I'm not sure. Is there any way to check which one it's under?

author_note: Could be product_issue or delivery damage. Cause is unstated.
text: The tableware set arrived but two of the side plates are chipped. Not sure if that happened in transit, the box looked fine. What's the process here?

author_note: Pre-purchase question that reads like a complaint. Low urgency, unclear category.
text: Is the Marlow armchair actually in stock? The site said 3-5 days when I looked on Tuesday and now it says 6 weeks. I haven't ordered yet but I'd like to know before I do.

author_note: Explicit injury from a product. Must escalate on product_safety, high urgency.
text: The glass shade on the pendant light we fitted last week shattered while my husband was changing the bulb. He's cut his hand quite badly, we've been to A&E. Order 46902. I want to know what you're going to do about this.

author_note: Electrical fault, no injury yet, calm tone, asks for nothing. Tests 'applies even when calm'.
text: Just to let you know, the table lamp from order 50441 gets extremely hot after about twenty minutes and there was a burning smell yesterday. I've unplugged it and put it in the garage. Not after a refund, just thought someone should know.

author_note: Child safety risk, structural. Must escalate.
text: The bunk bed ladder came away from the frame while my son was climbing down. Two of the fixing points had sheared clean off. He's fine but he could easily have broken something. This is order 48770 and I'm quite shaken by it.

author_note: Safety framed as a trivial complaint. Easy to under-triage.
text: Minor thing but the edge of the console table is really sharp where the veneer has lifted, I caught my arm on it and it drew blood. Probably just needs sanding? Order 51663.

author_note: Clear unauthorised access. Must escalate, high urgency.
text: Someone has been in my account. There's an order I didn't place going to an address in Manchester and my delivery address has been changed. I've not shared my password with anyone. Please stop that order and lock the account.

author_note: Phishing report. Security escalation, no order involved.
text: I've had an email that looks like it's from you asking me to confirm my card details via a link, but the address is hearthandloom-billing.net which doesn't look right. Did you send this? I haven't clicked anything.

author_note: Plain forgotten password. Must NOT escalate. Tests the explicit carve-out in the brief.
text: I've forgotten my password and the reset email isn't coming through. I've checked spam. Can you help me get back in? Account is under this email address.

author_note: Unrecognised charge. Security escalation.
text: There's a charge on my card from you for £212 dated the 8th and I haven't ordered anything since March. Can you tell me what this is? I've not authorised it.

author_note: Explicit chargeback threat over a modest amount.
text: I've asked four times for the refund on order 49001 and had nothing. If it isn't in my account by Friday I'm raising a chargeback with my bank and reporting you to Trading Standards.

author_note: Solicitor mentioned, calm and formal tone.
text: Further to my previous correspondence of 2 September, I have instructed a solicitor regarding the damaged sideboard supplied under order 47338 and the subsequent refusal to collect it. Please direct all further communication to them; details below.

author_note: Social media / press threat. Escalation on legal_or_chargeback_threat per the brief.
text: I have 40,000 followers and I am more than happy to tell every single one of them exactly how Hearth & Loom treats its customers. I've already drafted the post. Last chance to make this right.

author_note: Ombudsman reference inside an otherwise routine refund chase.
text: Could you confirm the status of my refund for order 50902 please. I've read that if it isn't resolved within eight weeks I can take it to the ombudsman, and we're at week six now.

author_note: £680 refund, calm, no other trigger. Must escalate on amount alone.
text: I'd like to return the Marlow three-seater sofa from order 46115. It's too large for the room. The order was £680. What do I need to do to arrange collection and get the money back?

author_note: £95 -- deliberately just UNDER the £100 threshold. Must NOT escalate on amount.
text: Hello, I'd like a refund on the Ashford wool rug, order 51877. It was £95 including delivery. It's unused and still in the original wrapping.

author_note: No figure stated, expensive-sounding item. Brief says do not infer an amount.
text: I want to send back the dining table from order 48219, it's not the colour I expected from the photos. How do I arrange a refund?

author_note: Amount split across two items summing over £100. Tests whether totalling happens.
text: Two things to return from order 52001 - the brass floor lamp at £74 and the pair of side tables at £58. Neither fits the space. Can I return both together?
